messages.settings.title: Settings
messages.settings.notice.plaintext: Settings are kept in this browser in plain text, including RPC URLs. Do not put a URL there that contains a secret you would not store in plain text. No key is ever stored.
messages.settings.rpc.hint: Only https:// and wss:// are accepted, with no username or password. The chain id is verified when the endpoint is used. No default RPC is built in.
messages.settings.rpc.connected: Connected. The endpoint reports the expected chain id.
messages.settings.rpc.failed: Failed: the endpoint is unreachable or reports a different chain.
messages.settings.rpc.secondary.label: {chain} second RPC URL (optional)
messages.settings.rpc.secondary.hint: A different provider. Scans compare it with the main RPC and withhold the checkpoint when they disagree.
messages.settings.relayer.label: Relayer URL (optional)
messages.settings.relayer.hint: https only. The relayer sees the one-time address, destination, token, amount and timing of each sweep it handles.
messages.settings.delay.range: Each payment is delayed between {min, number} and {max, number} seconds.
messages.settings.lock.label: Lock local tags after idle minutes
messages.settings.lock.hint: Keys stay in memory until you wipe them or close the tab.
messages.settings.lock.summary: Locks after {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} without activity.
messages.settings.theme.label: Theme
messages.settings.autoclear.label: Remove the invoice from the address bar after reading it
messages.settings.pins.label: Pinned seller signing keys (one per line)
messages.settings.pins.hint: Only keys you pin are described as pinned. Get them from the seller over a channel you trust.
messages.settings.pins.count: {count, plural, =0 {No pinned signer keys} one {# pinned signer key} other {# pinned signer keys}}
messages.settings.storageUnavailable: Browser storage is unavailable, so these settings apply to this tab only.
messages.settings.error.pins: Pinned signer keys must be 66 hexadecimal characters starting with 02 or 03, one per line.
messages.settings.error.lock: Lock timeout must be 1 to 240 minutes.

messages.sweep.tokenNotAllowed: This token is not on the allowlist. It will not be swept from here.
messages.sweep.payerFollow.title: The payer can follow this sweep
messages.sweep.payerFollow.body: The payer knows the one-time address. When you move its funds, the destination and everything else that address has received or will receive are public and linkable. Use a fresh destination for each sweep, and avoid an address already known to be yours if you do not want to link those funds. A relayer also sees your IP address (hashed), amount and timing. Your stealth key is derived in memory for this action and is never shown or stored.
messages.sweep.destination.label: Destination address (your own wallet)
messages.sweep.vaultPass.label: Vault passphrase (required for each sweep action)
messages.sweep.vaultPass.hint: Checked against the encrypted vault and the seller keys currently loaded. It is cleared after every action.
messages.sweep.vaultError: Could not check encrypted vault storage, so sweep signing is disabled until storage is available.
messages.sweep.feeLegend: How to pay the network fee
messages.sweep.modeRelayer: Through the relayer (fee deducted from the amount; needs a permit-capable token)
messages.sweep.modeDirect: Directly (the one-time address must hold native coin for gas)
messages.sweep.relayerNeeds: Relayer sweeps need a relayer URL in Settings and a token with ERC-2612 permit. Use a direct sweep otherwise.
messages.sweep.checkExplorer: Check it on your RPC or a block explorer you trust before relying on it.

messages.sellerKeys.keystoreDecrypted: Keystore decrypted; keys are in memory.

messages.sellerKeys.title: Seller keys
messages.sellerKeys.memory.title: Keys stay in memory by default
messages.sellerKeys.memory.body: Keys are generated and used only inside this page. They are never written to browser storage unless you explicitly save the optional encrypted vault below. Reloading or closing the tab forgets keys that were not saved.
messages.sellerKeys.checkingVault: Checking for an encrypted seller vault…
messages.sellerKeys.storageUnavailable.title: Encrypted browser storage is unavailable
messages.sellerKeys.storageUnavailable.body: This browser cannot read the optional vault. In-memory key use and encrypted file backups remain available, but do not try to save a local vault here.
messages.sellerKeys.vaultSavedHeading: Encrypted seller vault saved in this browser
messages.sellerKeys.unlockExplain: Unlocking replaces the keys currently in memory. The vault stores only the encrypted keystore text; your passphrase is never saved.
messages.sellerKeys.deleteExplain: This permanently deletes the saved ciphertext in this browser. Keep a separate backup first if needed.
messages.sellerKeys.signKey.label: Invoice-signing private key (optional)
messages.sellerKeys.signKey.hint: Leave empty to generate a separate signing key. It must not be your spending or viewing key.
messages.sellerKeys.metaShare: Share this to receive payments. It reveals no private key.
messages.sellerKeys.payersSee: “signature matches key …”. They can pin this key; an unpinned key identifies nobody.
messages.sellerKeys.formatNote: Format: scrypt (N=2^17, r=8, p=1) and AES-256-GCM. The passphrase is not stored anywhere.
messages.sellerKeys.forgetQr: Forget encrypted QR from this page
messages.sellerKeys.vaultExplain: This keeps an encrypted keystore in this browser’s IndexedDB so you can unlock after reload. Anyone with access to this browser profile can copy the ciphertext and attempt offline guesses; choose a strong passphrase. Browser storage can be cleared or lost, so keep a separate backup. GhostPay never saves the passphrase or plaintext key material here.
messages.sellerKeys.saveVault: Save encrypted vault in this browser
messages.sellerKeys.vaultExists: A vault already exists. It is never overwritten automatically; unlock or explicitly delete it before saving a different key set.
messages.sellerKeys.registryHint: Publishing your meta-address to the ERC-6538 registry would publicly associate it with your wallet address. Publishing is optional and has its own page.
messages.settings.outside.title: Settings can be changed outside this page
messages.settings.outside.body: Anything that can write to this site’s browser storage, including another local user, malware or an extension, can change these RPC, relayer and pinned-signer settings. Review the endpoints and signer keys before relying on them. A second RPC can reveal disagreements, but it does not make either provider trustworthy by itself.
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.errWindow: Window size must be a whole number of blocks from 0 to 100000.
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.errDelays: Delays must be whole milliseconds, minimum at most maximum, up to 10000.
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.errBudget: The per-scan budget must be from 1 to 100000.
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.saved: Scan privacy settings saved. They apply to the next scan.
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.refused: This browser refused to store the scan privacy settings.
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.hint: These options change how announcements are fetched, not what is on-chain. A web page cannot open a SOCKS connection or check that it runs in Tor Browser: “Tor Browser” means you opened this page in Tor Browser yourself; “Local proxy” means a JSON-RPC forwarder you run on this computer (for example one that sends traffic over Tor). Defaults add no new destination.
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.requireProxy: Require the private path (block the scan instead of falling back; skip the direct second RPC behind a local proxy)
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.endpointRequired: Required: an address on 127.0.0.1 or localhost.
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.endpointOptional: Optional: leave empty to use the RPC above.
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.sourceIndexer: Public-log indexer (block hashes checked against your RPC)
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.windowHint: Everyone using the same window sends identical range queries. Capped at the chain's log range.
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.budgetHint: Announcements posted by the GhostPay router are always checked first. Others beyond this budget are deferred to the next scan, never skipped.

messages.about.title: About and privacy
messages.about.intro: GhostPay creates one-time (stealth) addresses so that a seller’s receiving address is not published. It is a static page: there is no GhostPay server, account or analytics, and it loads no third-party code or fonts.
messages.about.feeNote: Gas-sponsored sweeps charge max(110 % of the gas cost, 0.5 % of the amount), capped at 3 %, shown in the quote before you sign. The optional gas buffer and the delay are free.
messages.about.verify.title: How to verify this release
messages.about.verify.intro: The SHA-256 on Home is informational: this page computes it from a script fetched from the same host. A compromised host could serve both the app and the hash it wants you to see, so that check does not establish that the release is authentic.
messages.about.verify.step1: Download the published release and its checksum from a second channel, then verify the files locally with the published SHA256SUMS.
messages.about.verify.step2: When a release key is built into this app, the deployment manifest must have a valid signature from one of those keys. That signature only helps if you have verified the app bundle itself.
messages.about.verify.step3: Check that the deployment addresses and code match the chain through an RPC you trust. A second independent RPC can expose disagreements, but agreement alone does not prove either provider is honest.
messages.about.verify.step4: Before sending, check that the final screen and your wallet show the same contract, one-time address, amounts and fee recipient.
messages.about.verify.step5: Hosting headers such as CSP and Referrer-Policy only apply on hosts that support them; static hosts may not be able to enforce every policy.
messages.about.noAudit: No external audit of this software has been performed.
